summary: Revenue reached €1,503M (+7.7% at constant exchange rates) and group RevPAR rose 4.9%. Luxury & Lifestyle RevPAR grew 8.3%, 11.3% excluding the Middle East, where UAE RevPAR is still down about 20%. The 2026 EBITDA target moves up to €1,270–1,285M.
title: Accor Q3: luxury RevPAR up 8.9%, full-year target raised
why: Luxury pricing power holds; the Gulf is the drag. A benchmark for 2027 budgets in Paris, the Riviera and Dubai.
body_long:
Accor's luxury hotels were the stand-out of its third quarter. In results published on 22 October 2026, the group reported revenue of €1,503 million, up 7.7% at constant exchange rates, and group RevPAR up 4.9%.

## Luxury leads

The Luxury & Lifestyle division grew revenue 11.6% at constant exchange rates, to €404 million. Its RevPAR rose 8.3%, or 11.3% excluding the Middle East, driven mainly by price. Within it, the luxury brands, which account for 71% of the division, posted RevPAR up 8.9%, with occupancy at 69.0% and an average rate of €275, up 7.2%. Every luxury brand and region grew except the Middle East.

The Premium, Midscale and Economy division grew RevPAR 3.2%, with revenue of €767 million.

## Europe and the Gulf

In Europe and North Africa, RevPAR rose 2.5%. France, which accounts for 43% of the region, saw slight growth over the summer before a strong September, helped by Céline Dion's concerts, the papal visit and trade fairs. The UK was resilient, and Germany's September RevPAR grew almost double digits on a strong events calendar.

The United Arab Emirates was the only market hit by the regional conflict, with RevPAR down about 20% year on year, although improving on the second quarter. Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Turkey led growth in the Middle East and Africa, and Southeast Asia, led by Japan, Indonesia and Thailand, was the group's growth engine in Asia.

## Network and outlook

Accor opened 63 hotels and nearly 9,000 rooms in the quarter. At the end of September it operated 5,857 hotels with 885,219 rooms, and its pipeline reached more than 273,000 rooms, up 9.5%.

The group raised its 2026 target for current EBITDA to €1,270 million to €1,285 million, and expects RevPAR growth in the upper part of its 2% to 2.5% range, assuming no deterioration in the UAE in the fourth quarter. Chairman and CEO Sébastien Bazin said the performance, led by Luxury & Lifestyle and a favourable events calendar, allowed the group to raise its targets despite an uncertain geopolitical context.

## The signal

Luxury pricing power is intact in Europe: rates are still rising faster than occupancy. The Gulf remains the drag, but it is improving. For general managers in Paris, on the Riviera and in Dubai, these figures are a useful benchmark for 2027 budgets.

visual_text.rest: lifts luxury RevPAR 8.9% in the third quarter.
